policy: Every raw production filesystem mutation source is count-pinned here. Authoritative files use atomic sibling promotion; stronger tree, archive, append-log, SQLite, retention, ephemeral, and fixture contracts remain explicit exceptions.

writers.rationale: The composition root contains guarded atomic source/snapshot writes, verified deployment/release directory transactions, isolated compilation/release materializers, bounded snapshot/artifact retention, and embedded scratch-only route fixtures including the isolated provider-dispatch evidence marker.
writers.failureContract: Authoritative files preserve prior bytes; tree promotion rolls back; scratch trees never target configured live roots; retention deletes only named bounded artifacts; the provider-dispatch marker requires non-production plus explicit route-test mode, writes fixed-name non-secret evidence only beneath the harness-provided isolated fixture directory, and propagates append failure so the oracle cannot report false success.

writers.rationale: Creates canonical, corrupt, tampered, unavailable-root, and junction-escape fixtures only beneath unique temporary roots; extra mkdir/symlink calls construct isolated physical-ancestor realpath-EPERM and link-refusal fixtures beneath unique temporary roots.
writers.failureContract: Fixture cleanup is best effort; the physical-ancestor realpath-EPERM and link-refusal fixtures never target production data, receipts, history, or configured workspace paths.

writers.rationale: Stores canonical receipt bytes through a sibling temporary file, fsync, and atomic rename under the relocatable receipt root.
writers.failureContract: Root, ID, symlink/junction, corrupt-byte, and write failures fail closed; a pre-promotion failure leaves the prior receipt bytes untouched and cleans the temporary file.

writers.rationale: Creates a torn JSONL tail only inside a unique temporary fixture.
writers.failureContract: Fixture cleanup is best effort and production history is never opened.

writers.rationale: Content-addressed blobs use write-then-rename while ledger rows are append-only JSONL with bounded rotated segments.
writers.failureContract: Torn final rows are ignored by the reader; blob hashes never name partial bytes; history failure never fabricates revertibility.

writers.rationale: Production key state delegates to restricted atomic JSON; remaining raw writes corrupt and clean only a temporary negative fixture.
writers.failureContract: Create, revoke, and prune commit or keep prior memory/disk state; audit touch failure rolls memory back without changing authority.

writers.rationale: Writes only a caller-created empty artifact stage and hash-verifies every copied loose file before promotion elsewhere.
writers.failureContract: Any copy/hash/catalog error marks the stage failed; callers discard the isolated tree and never promote it.

writers.rationale: Materializes a complete plan only into a new or empty stage and reopens every destination for size and SHA verification.
writers.failureContract: A partial stage returns failure and is never accepted or promoted by deployment/release callers.

writers.rationale: Creates the cache directory; database durability is separately inventoried as WAL plus explicit transactions and generation visibility.
writers.failureContract: Database open/migration failure degrades to the in-memory cache; the selftest root is disposable.

writers.rationale: Recovery metadata is atomic JSON; payload trees are exact pre-state copies; raw writes construct corrupt/restore fixtures only.
writers.failureContract: A receipt is never advertised until payload and record verify; corrupt, expired, oversized, stale, and replayed receipts refuse.

writers.rationale: Address-only discovery records use restricted atomic writes; raw calls remove dead or shutting-down instance pointers.
writers.failureContract: Discovery failure is fail-soft for server startup, but torn records cannot replace a valid record and dead PIDs are never returned.

writers.rationale: Builds only temporary fake game/live/corpus path-role fixtures.
writers.failureContract: No configured path is read or written and the unique temporary root is removed.

writers.rationale: Raw writes create bounded manifest, binary, image, and executable-signature fixtures in a temporary root.
writers.failureContract: Production release preparation is read-only in this module; all fixture bytes are deleted after the oracle.

writers.rationale: Creates a disposable mod-tree fixture to prove hashing and exclusion behavior.
writers.failureContract: The scanner is read-only in production and cleanup targets only its unique temp root.

writers.rationale: Creates and removes a disposable vanilla/DLC reference corpus fixture.
writers.failureContract: Production corpus indexing is read-only and cache invalidation never mutates the corpus.

writers.rationale: Asynchronous filesystem mutations build and remove only a unique temporary reference-manifest fixture.
writers.failureContract: Production manifest generation is read-only and the fixture root is never a configured corpus or workspace.

writers.rationale: Builds a disposable base/DLC overlay fixture and removes one DLC to prove refresh.
writers.failureContract: Production overlay resolution is read-only; the temp root is always cleaned.

writers.rationale: Creates bounded cursor/session, corruption, and failed-promotion fixtures only beneath one unique temporary root.
writers.failureContract: Fixture cleanup is best effort; persisted-session corruption and promotion-failure fixtures never target configured data, workspace, game, mod, or corpus roots.

writers.rationale: Creates validated runtime debug session root segments; persisted bounded session JSON delegates to the shared atomic writer.
writers.failureContract: Filesystem-root, forbidden-root, non-directory, link, and unavailable-root checks refuse unsafe state roots; atomic promotion preserves prior session bytes on failure.

writers.rationale: Writes only temporary XSD include/import fixtures.
writers.failureContract: Schema discovery is read-only in production and fixture cleanup is confined to its temp root.

writers.rationale: Writes only generated XSD routing fixtures in a unique temporary directory.
writers.failureContract: Production routing reads supplied schemas and never mutates them.

writers.rationale: Production baselines delegate to atomic JSON; the raw write deliberately corrupts a temp fixture.
writers.failureContract: Corrupt state is unavailable and refuses overwrite; promotion occurs only after explicitly green validation.

writers.rationale: This is the shared sibling-temp atomic authority; extra raw calls exercise corruption/failure and prune old parked states.
writers.failureContract: Complete bytes and requested restricted mode exist before rename; failure preserves the destination and cleans the unique temp.

writers.rationale: Registry index and records use the shared atomic writer; create removes an unindexed new record when index promotion fails, while compensateCreate validates paired identity and hashes, promotes removal from the index, and unlinks only a strictly guarded just-created record; remaining raw calls build corruption and migration fixtures in a unique temporary root.
writers.failureContract: Create rollback removes only the newly written unindexed record when index promotion fails; compensateCreate verifies paired identity, hashes, and regular-file state, promotes the index first, and attempts exact prior-index restoration if record cleanup fails, reporting partial state when restoration cannot be established; fixture mutations never reach configured state.

writers.rationale: Catalog volumes are streamed to exclusive temp files inside an isolated artifact stage, then renamed; remaining raw writes are parser fixtures.
writers.failureContract: Partial CAT/DAT temps are removed; callers verify the complete staged catalogs before any tree promotion.

owners: B119 configured-census physical reparse containment test
writers.rationale: All files and links are created beneath one unique OS temporary root to prove selected-root link admission and child-reparse escape refusal.
writers.failureContract: Finally cleanup is bounded to that unique OS temporary root and no configured workspace/corpus/game/mod path is mutated.

writers.rationale: Production config delegates to atomic replacement; raw calls create valid/corrupt temporary XSD/config fixtures.
writers.failureContract: A failed settings save preserves prior config bytes; fixture corruption never reaches the normal config root.

writers.rationale: Writes only a temporary schema fixture for validator coverage.
writers.failureContract: Production schema validation is read-only and cleanup is temp-root confined.

writers.rationale: Production credentials use restricted atomic JSON; the raw write creates a corrupt negative fixture only.
writers.failureContract: Corrupt stores refuse mutation and failed promotion preserves every previous credential.

writers.rationale: Creates one unique temporary root for workspace-registry, action-receipt, recovery, and bulk-transform apply receipt adapter fixtures.
writers.failureContract: Fixture cleanup is best effort; selftest mutations never target configured workspace, registry, receipt, recovery, or production roots.

writers.rationale: Creates the bounded harvested-schema root; every schema file is written through atomic sibling promotion.
writers.failureContract: A failed extraction/write is reported missing and cannot leave a torn schema file.

writers.rationale: Credential values use restricted atomic JSON; raw calls enforce mode and explicitly delete the credential on user request.
writers.failureContract: Set failure preserves prior credential; delete reports failure and never returns a false configured state.

writers.rationale: Writes only disposable plain/gzip/corrupt save fixtures for identity correlation.
writers.failureContract: Production identity probes read user-selected saves only and never mutate them.

writers.rationale: Creates disposable debug-log and corrupt persisted-session fixtures beneath one unique temporary adapter root and appends bounded log evidence for selection and rotation cases.
writers.failureContract: Fixture cleanup is best effort; every log and store mutation remains under the unique temporary root and never targets configured game, mod, corpus, workspace, or production roots.

writers.rationale: Creates one unique temporary workspace-registry and action-receipt fixture root for the adapter selftest.
writers.failureContract: Fixture cleanup is best effort; selftest mutations never target configured workspace, registry, receipt, or production roots.

writers.rationale: Creates snapshot-restore source and fault fixtures only beneath one unique OS temporary root and removes that root in the selftest finally block.
writers.failureContract: The selftest reports failed checks or an unexpected adapter failure; fixture cleanup is attempted in finally, and fixture mutations never target configured workspace, registry, receipt, recovery, or production roots.

writers.rationale: Validates an explicit physical extensions root and stages an exact signed merge-law fixture through a guarded sibling transaction before promotion and cleanup.
writers.failureContract: Unsafe, conflicting, foreign, or malformed targets refuse before mutation; write or promotion failures roll back owned state or report guarded residue, and cleanup reports incomplete state after a post-mutation failure without touching unowned files.

writers.rationale: This is the extension-host sibling-stage and multi-file rollback authority; raw calls also drive its isolated failure fixture.
writers.failureContract: All bytes stage first; partial promotion restores every previous file and preserves an unrecoverable backup instead of deleting it.

writers.rationale: Creates isolated extension global-storage state/config/data roots before the managed sidecar starts.
writers.failureContract: Directory creation failure prevents sidecar startup and is surfaced through the extension error path.

writers.rationale: Production JSON files delegate to the extension atomic helper; remaining raw mutations construct merge/corruption fixtures.
writers.failureContract: Failed promotion preserves existing VS Code settings/recommendations and temporary fixtures never use a real mod.

writers.rationale: Creates only disposable release ZIP/tool/command fixtures.
writers.failureContract: No native dialog or user output path is touched and the unique temporary root is removed.

writers.rationale: User-selected release ZIP export copies to an exclusive sibling temp, checks receipt hash/size, backs up an existing target, promotes, reopens, and rolls back.
writers.failureContract: Any mismatch or promotion error reports failure and restores the prior selected output; final success names verified bytes only.

hostStores.rationale: Browser storage mirrors server-owned workspace/release state by immutable ID or retains non-authoritative UI preferences and acknowledgements.
hostStores.failureContract: Authoritative state remains on the server; preference failures keep current in-memory behavior and never authorize a write.

hostStores.rationale: Removes obsolete browser OAuth identity metadata after the server-owned credential migration.
hostStores.failureContract: Removal failure cannot expose a current provider credential because tokens are no longer stored there.

hostStores.rationale: Caches only the last reviewer label; the guarded server route revalidates every suppression authority field.
hostStores.failureContract: Failure loses convenience text only and cannot weaken validation or commit a suppression.

hostStores.rationale: Stores a presentation preference with no source, deployment, credential, or authority meaning.
hostStores.failureContract: Failure falls back to the default display mode without changing project data.

owners: GitHub repository preference and legacy-token cleanup
hostStores.rationale: Caches display history and repository selections; credentials are server-owned and browser PAT remnants are deletion-only.
hostStores.failureContract: Browser cache failure cannot perform Git or network mutation and server routes re-check credentials and requested operations.

hostStores.rationale: Stores only virtualized toolbox presentation state.
hostStores.failureContract: Failure retains the current session state or restores the default view.

hostStores.rationale: Stores user-authored snippet convenience data that is not compiled or deployed without a later explicit project action.
hostStores.failureContract: Storage exceptions surface through the owning UI path and cannot mutate workspace or deployed files.

hostStores.rationale: Keeps non-secret provider/model choices and deletes legacy browser key values; current credentials are server-owned.
hostStores.failureContract: Preference failure uses defaults; key cleanup failure never makes browser keys authoritative or eligible for implicit dispatch.

hostStores.rationale: Caches an uncommitted blueprint draft for browser continuity.
hostStores.failureContract: Failure can lose the draft cache but cannot create, compile, deploy, or publish a mod.

hostStores.rationale: Keeps the server-injected token and generated client/workspace selection within the current browser tab rather than durable local storage.
hostStores.failureContract: Failure leaves API calls unauthorized or forces a fresh server bootstrap; a stale workspace selection is removed only after the server refuses it and is never downgraded into persistent storage.

hostStores.rationale: Stores the last selected immutable workspace ID for restart bootstrap plus non-authoritative adoption/decline/refusal/conflict counters in IDE-managed global state.
hostStores.failureContract: Workspace selection is accepted only after the authenticated backend binds the ID; persistence failure fails that host handoff or falls back to safe bootstrap on restart, while telemetry never changes authorization or source state.

browserOutputs.rationale: Hands a non-authoritative JSON representation of the current workspace to the browser download manager after an explicit user action.
browserOutputs.failureContract: Download failure cannot mutate the server workspace, compiled artifacts, deployment state, credentials, or game files.

owners: verified Nexus and Steam artifact export
browserOutputs.rationale: Exports only server-prepared artifacts whose size and SHA-256 match the release receipt; the File System Access path reopens and reverifies saved bytes while the fallback is explicitly an unreceipted browser handoff.
browserOutputs.failureContract: Picker cancellation or write/hash failure preserves the verified internal artifact and reports no successful export; browser-download fallback states that the final destination cannot be reopened or receipted.

database.failureContract: SQLite WAL owns page durability; migrations, game-root rebinding, multi-row replacements, and their visibility metadata use explicit transactions; long reference scans stay invisible until their generation becomes ready; the database is a disposable cache and falls back to memory.
